newsitem.title: ITALY: Former Italian rail chief granted house arrest.
newsitem.headline: Former Italian rail chief granted house arrest.

text.p: The former head of Italian state railway, Lorenzo Necci, was granted house arrest on Saturday after being jailed for more than six weeks in a corruption probe.
His lawyers said Necci would be released from the jail in this northwest town later on Saturday and would return to his home in Rome.
The preliminary examining judge who granted house arrest did not immediately release reasons for her ruling.
Necci, 55, was arrested on September 15, on the orders of La Spezia magistrates investigating an alleged corrupt "super lobby" in state industries and the judiciary.
He has been held on suspicion of committing a raft of corruption-related offences and resigned as managing director of the state railway after his arrest. He has denied wrongdoing.
The affair has mushroomed to include judges, businessmen and lawyers as magistrates probe allegations of trial-fixing, illegal arms exports and widespread bribes for state contracts.
Newspapers have dubbed the case "Tangentopoli 2", an echo of the "Tangentopoli" (Bribesville) corruption scandal which exploded in 1992 and buried Italy's governing elite.
